name: Alexander
overview: Alexander is a male figure noted in the New Testament for being handed over to Satan by the Apostle Paul as recorded in 1 Timothy 1:20. He is also identified as a coppersmith in 2 Timothy 4:14. No tribal affiliation is recorded for him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Alexander is presented plainly without a given meaning or divine origin in the biblical text. It is a proper name mentioned specifically in 1 Timothy 1:20.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Alexander beyond what is noted in his unique attribute of being disciplined by Paul.
scriptureSignificance: Alexander's significance lies primarily in his negative example within the early church, as Paul mentions him in the context of church discipline. Being handed over to Satan indicates a serious corrective action meant to bring about repentance. His profession as a coppersmith may suggest his social context but is secondary to his role in the apostolic admonition.
